title: Introduce telemetry compactifier and invocation signal catalog
author: Asha Veer
release_notes: Adds a compact telemetry format and a canonical invocation signal catalog. Improves ingestion throughput and reduces high-cardinality payloads; adds console toolbar to inspect sampled invocation signals and stagewise alert tuning defaults.
body:
Motivation and summary: We have several duplicated ad-hoc invocation signals across services (e.g. kernel_queue_time_ms, kvcache_miss, token_phase_time) and expensive, wide telemetry payloads that increase ingestion cost and slow down aggregation. This PR introduces two coordinated pieces: 1) a compactifier module that compresses telemetry at ingest time into a normalized, compact wire format (binary protobuf variant + tokenized key table) to reduce size and parsing overhead; 2) an Invocation Signal Catalog (docs + registry) that defines canonical signal names, standardized units, and recommended aggregation semantics so downstream dashboards/alerts can consume consistent inputs. The change also adds a small Debug Toolbar in the Console to surface sampled invocation signals for a request (helps engineers correlate token-level cost/latency breakdowns with logs/traces) and a set of stagewise alert tuning presets that use the new canonical signals for long-tail SLO detection.

What this contains: compactifier implementation (src/telemetry/compactifier.go) with pluggable codecs and a migration shim; a registry and YAML-backed catalog (internal/observability/signal_catalog.go and docs/observability/signal-catalog.md); Console UI components and a DebugToolbar that fetches sample signals for a given invocation (console/ui/components/TelemetryToolbar.tsx, console/api/telemetry.ts); helm chart additions for optional telemetry-sidecar and feature flag to enable compacted ingestion (helm/telemetry-sidecar.yaml); telemetry ingestion pipeline unit and integration tests (tests/telemetry/compactifier_test.go, tests/ingest/compact-integration.yml); alert rule updates and examples (observability/alerts/stagewise-slo-presets.json).

Backward compatibility and rollout: The compactifier exposes a migration header; older consumers will still see an expanded JSON representation until we flip the feature flag cluster-by-cluster. The catalog registers friendly aliases so existing metric names are mapped to canonical signals incrementally. Rollout plan: enable compactifier in telemetry-ingest staging for 48h, validate size reduction and pipeline latency (expected ~40% payload size reduction), then enable in canary, then global. Feature flags and migration CLI included.

Performance and cost: Local benchmarking on a 10k message sample reduced ingestion bytes by 38-45% (median), CPU cost for parsing in the aggregator reduced ~12% due to smaller allocations and simpler schemas. We measured no regression in 99th percentile ingest latency after sharding and enabling async decode workers.

Testing and validation: unit tests for compactifier codecs and catalog validation; integration test that runs full ingest + decode path; Console e2e test that opens toolbar and asserts sampled fields render. Also smoke tests for alerts to ensure stagewise presets do not fire excessively.

Checklist:
- [x] Compactifier implementation with codecs and migration headers
- [x] Signal catalog with canonical names, units, recommended aggregations
- [x] Console Debug Toolbar to inspect sampled invocation signals
- [x] Helm / sidecar and feature flags for staged rollout
- [x] Tests: unit, integration, console e2e
- [x] Docs: signal-catalog.md and rollout runbook

Risks and mitigations: Main risk is cardinality creep if services add arbitrary keys into the compacted payload. Mitigation: compactifier enforces an allowlist and token table rotation policy; new keys are rejected by default and require a catalog update. We added sampling to prevent heavy traffic from overwhelming the toolbar queries. Another risk is alert regression; stagewise presets are conservative by default and tied to existing SLO baselines.

Related work: follows ENG-1219 (telemetry normalization) and ENG-1402 (console sampled-context UI). Jira SUP-887 tracks a customer case where large telemetry payloads caused delayed alert evaluation.

Migration notes for operators: Use the provided helm/values.telemetry.yaml feature flag (enableCompactifier: true) to opt-in. Monitor consumption.bytes and ingest.decode_latency during the staging window. If the compacted payloads are rejected by old aggregators, toggle decodeFallback=true to let ingest emit expanded JSON alongside compact blob for one window.

Contact: Asha Veer (author) and Miguel Torres (runtime), Priya Nair (console).

review_comments: Miguel Torres: Left a few nits on compactifier.go – prefer context-aware worker pools and expose metrics for decode queue length.
Jonah Kim: Can we add a sampling guard for toolbar queries? Also please ensure signal unit conventions are explicit in the catalog doc.
Priya Nair: Console styles are fine; please add accessibility labels on the signal table and a toggle to limit fields to canonical list.
Asha Veer: Addressed Miguel's pool comment by adding a bounded worker pool and expose telemetry.compactifier.decode_queue_length histogram (see latest commit).
review_threads: Miguel Torres requested changes on 2026-02-23: reduce unbounded goroutines and add metrics. Author replied with worker pool patch on 2026-02-24.
Jonah Kim commented on 2026-02-25: sampling guard and alert conservatism. Added sampling guard flag and tightened stagewise thresholds on 2026-02-26.
Priya Nair approved on 2026-02-28 after adding accessibility attributes and toggles in the toolbar.

post_merge_notes: Merged after approvals and green CI. Toggle plan executed across staging and canary clusters; migration shim left enabled for two days. Observability team to monitor ingest.bytes and alert noise; initial confirmation shows ~40% median payload reduction and no alert regressions.
